title: Docker deployment
description: Run the API with persistent storage and put your own HTTPS endpoint in front of it.

sections.title: Build the image
paragraphs: Run these commands from the loft repository. This uses the storage API Dockerfile, not a hosted loft service.
sections.code:
docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile -t loft-api .
docker volume create loft-data

sections.title: Start with persistent disk storage
paragraphs: Set your credentials before starting the container. The named volume preserves file data, metadata, and issued links when the container is replaced. The port binds to loopback so a reverse proxy can expose it.
sections.code:
export LOFT_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
export LOFT_SIGNING_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
docker run -d --name loft-api --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8787:8787 \
  -v loft-data:/data \
  -e LOFT_DATA=/data -e LOFT_TOKEN -e LOFT_SIGNING_KEY \
  -e LOFT_ORIGIN=https://api.example.com \
  -e LOFT_WEB=https://files.example.com \
  loft-api

sections.title: Add HTTPS and verify
paragraphs: Replace the example domains with your own. Configure a TLS reverse proxy to forward your API hostname to 127.0.0.1:8787. Allow the request sizes and transfer durations your files need.
LOFT_ORIGIN describes the API origin; it does not configure TLS. LOFT_WEB is the origin of your self-hosted web pages for issued links.

sections.title: Operate one writer per store
paragraphs: Run one API writer against a given store. Metadata and link updates are serialized within one process; multiple writers need transactional coordination that is not currently implemented.

Back up the volume and preserve your credentials in a secret manager. The repository’s development Compose file does not currently attach its declared named volume to the API service; use the explicit volume mount above for persistence.
